The challenge

What makes marketplaces & platforms different.

01

Supply applications and documents arrive by form, email and WhatsApp, and verification quality depends on who is on shift.

02

Prohibited items, off-platform contact details and fake reviews reach the live site before anyone looks at them.

03

New demand waits without a response because suitable providers never hear about it.

04

Grievance timelines under India's amended IT Rules and seller disclosure duties under the amended E-Commerce Rules need tracked processes, not inbox habits.

Where automation helps

Practical uses for marketplaces & platforms.

01

Seller and provider verification

Check GSTIN, PAN and bank details through your verification provider, extract license fields from documents, and send each application to a reviewer with a checklist.

02

Listing and review moderation

Hold risky listings, reviews and messages for review using rules and a moderation model, and record each decision with a policy reason and an appeal route.

03

Demand-to-supply alerts

Notify matching providers when a new request fits their category, area and availability, and alert operations when a request stays unfilled past the agreed time.

04

Grievance tracking

Log user complaints with acknowledgment and resolution deadlines, assign them to the grievance officer's queue and report on timeliness each month.

05

Marketplace health reporting

Report GMV, take rate, fill rate and repeat usage from reconciled payment and order data in the monthly investor update.

Supply-side onboarding and verification queue

Seller, provider or host applications are collected in one structured flow, checked automatically where a reliable source exists, and decided by a reviewer working from a checklist in a single queue.

Marketplaces & platforms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Applications arrive through forms, email and WhatsApp with missing documents. Reviewers retype details, checks vary by person, and good suppliers wait weeks while incomplete applications are chased by hand.

Trigger

A new or updated supply application submitted through the marketplace's onboarding form or partner app.

How it runs

  • Collect the application in one form with a clear notice of what is checked and why, asking only for the documents the verification policy needs.
  • Validate GSTIN, PAN and bank account details through the client's verification provider and flag duplicates against existing accounts.
  • Extract fields from licenses or certificates with an AI model, showing each field beside its source image with a confidence flag.
  • Place the application in a Retool review queue with a checklist, prior history and a suggested next action.
  • On approval, create the payout account in Stripe Connect or Razorpay Route and start first-listing tasks; on gaps, request the missing item by email or by an approved WhatsApp template where the applicant opted in.
  • Track application age and rework reasons in a weekly operations view.

Human checkpoint

A trained operations reviewer approves, rejects or requests more information for every application. The model never rejects anyone, and high-risk categories and appeals go to a senior reviewer.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Marketplace admin and database
  • KYC and GSTIN verification API
  • Stripe Connect or Razorpay Route

Data & consent

Identity and bank documents are sensitive: they are stored encrypted, only named reviewers can open them, every view is logged, and images go only to a model endpoint set for no training and limited retention. Rejected applicants' files are deleted on a defined schedule, subject to the payment partner's record-keeping duties.

What we deliver

  • Verification policy and reviewer checklist
  • Structured application flow
  • Retool review queue with audit log
  • Payout account creation workflow
  • Weekly onboarding operations view

How we measure it

  • Application-to-live time
  • Verification backlog age
  • Rework rate on applications
  • Issues found after approval

Two-sided matching alerts

New demand is matched against providers' saved criteria and availability, the best-fit providers are notified on the channel they chose, and operations steps in when a request stays unfilled.

Marketplaces & platforms

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Requests sit unanswered because suitable providers never see them, while active providers are flooded with irrelevant alerts and start ignoring all of them. Operations finds unfilled requests only when buyers complain.

Trigger

A new request, booking or job posted on the demand side, or a new listing that matches a buyer's saved search.

How it runs

  • Match the request against provider categories, service area, availability and capacity stored in the marketplace database.
  • Rank candidates with transparent rules such as distance, response history and rating, and label any sponsored placement as sponsored.
  • Notify the top candidates by push, email or an approved WhatsApp template according to each provider's opt-in, with a daily cap per provider.
  • Show the requester how many providers were notified and when responses arrive, without exposing providers who do not respond.
  • Alert the operations team in Slack when a request has no response within the agreed time, so a person can source supply.

Human checkpoint

Operations staff handle unfilled and high-value requests personally. The marketplace lead reviews ranking rules for fairness and approves any change to how providers are ordered.

Tools

Systems it connects

  • Marketplace database
  • Push notification service
  • Search and ranking service

Data & consent

Uses request category, area-level location, availability and response history. Exact addresses are shared only after a match is accepted. Alert preferences and opt-outs are honored per channel, and alert logs are kept for an agreed period so fairness can be reviewed.

What we deliver

  • Matching and ranking rules
  • Alert workflow with per-channel caps
  • Unfilled-request escalation in Slack
  • Liquidity view by category and city

How we measure it

  • Fill rate within the agreed time
  • Time to first provider response
  • Alert opt-out rate

Trust and safety moderation queue

Listings, reviews, profiles and messages are screened with rules and a moderation model, risky items are held for trained moderators, and every decision, notice and appeal is recorded with a policy reason.

Marketplaces & platforms · Consumer & mobile apps

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Prohibited items, fake reviews, harassment and off-platform contact details reach users before anyone checks. User reports pile up in an inbox, decisions vary by moderator, and the team cannot show how fast complaints were handled.

Trigger

New or edited user content, a user report, or a complaint sent to the grievance officer.

How it runs

  • Run rule checks such as banned-item terms, phone numbers in listings and price outliers, then a moderation model on text and images.
  • Publish low-risk items, hold medium-risk items for review, and block high-risk items until a moderator decides.
  • Show each item in a Retool queue with the policy clause, user history and prior reports, sorted by severity and deadline.
  • Record the moderator's decision with a reason code, notify the user and offer an appeal route.
  • Track complaints against the IT Rules timelines: acknowledgment within 24 hours and resolution within seven days, with faster handling for the categories the Rules specify.
  • Review overturned decisions monthly to tune rules and model thresholds.

Human checkpoint

Trained moderators decide removals and warnings; suspensions and bans need a senior reviewer. Law enforcement requests and legal notices go to the grievance officer and counsel, never to automation.

Tools

OOpenAIRRetoolSSupabasenn8nSSlack

Systems it connects

  • Marketplace or app content database
  • Help desk with grievance queue
  • In-app report and block features

Data & consent

Moderators see user content and reporter identity, so access is role-based and logged, and reporters are never revealed to the reported user. Graphic images are blurred by default in the queue. Decision logs are kept for the period the client's counsel sets for legal defense and regulatory requests.

What we deliver

  • Content policy mapped to reason codes
  • Screening rules and model thresholds
  • Retool moderation and appeal queue
  • Grievance timeline tracker
  • Monthly moderation quality review

How we measure it

  • Report-to-action time
  • Grievances resolved within deadline
  • Appeal overturn rate
  • Harmful items found after publishing

Docs-grounded support assistant with human handoff

An assistant that answers how-to questions only from your current docs and changelog, cites its sources, says it is an AI, and hands billing, account, security and uncertain cases to a person with a summary.

B2B SaaS · Marketplaces & platforms · AI-first products

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

The same setup and how-to questions fill the queue, so urgent bugs and billing problems wait. Generic chatbots answer from stale or invented information and trap users who need a person.

Trigger

A new conversation or ticket in the help desk or in-app chat.

How it runs

  • Classify intent, product area, urgency, plan tier and language.
  • Retrieve passages from approved help center articles, API docs, the changelog and known-issues pages, indexed with LlamaIndex in Qdrant.
  • Answer how-to questions with cited links and an AI disclosure; when no approved source supports an answer, say so and offer a person.
  • Route refunds, billing disputes, account access, security reports, data deletion requests and low-confidence cases to the human queue with a summary.
  • Turn reproducible bug reports into Jira issues with steps, environment and affected accounts.
  • Review a weekly sample of conversations and unanswered questions to fix docs and retrieval.

Human checkpoint

Support agents own every refund, account change, security report and data request. The support lead approves which sources the assistant may use and reviews the weekly sample before its scope expands.

Tools

OOpenAIACAnthropic ClaudeLLlamaIndexQQdrantnn8nJJiraSSlack

Systems it connects

  • Intercom, Zendesk or Freshdesk
  • Help center and API docs
  • Status page

Data & consent

Ticket text can contain personal data and secrets, so API keys, card numbers and passwords are redacted before model calls. Model providers are configured not to train on the data where that option exists. Conversation retention follows the help desk policy, and users see an AI disclosure at the first message.

What we deliver

  • Approved knowledge source list and index
  • Assistant with disclosure, citations and handoff
  • Escalation rules and agent summary format
  • Weekly quality review sheet

How we measure it

  • First response time
  • Resolution time
  • AI escalation rate
  • Groundedness of cited answers
  • Satisfaction on AI-handled conversations

Learn, ship & reportStandard3–5 weeks

Monthly investor and board metrics update

Revenue, pipeline, product and cost data are calculated with agreed definitions after month-end close, reconciled against the books, and drafted into an update the founder edits and sends.

B2B SaaS · Marketplaces & platforms · AI-first products

Open the automation blueprint

The problem

Founders spend days each month stitching numbers from Stripe, the CRM, product analytics and accounting exports. Definitions drift between months, and investors notice when MRR or GMV does not match the books.

Trigger

The finance lead confirming month-end close on the close checklist, or a fixed working day after month-end agreed with the founder.

How it runs

  • Load Stripe or Razorpay payments, CRM pipeline, PostHog usage and an accounting export into BigQuery.
  • Calculate metrics in dbt with locked definitions: MRR movements and net revenue retention, GMV and take rate for marketplaces, inference cost and gross margin for AI products.
  • Reconcile billing revenue with the accounting export and list differences for finance to explain.
  • Refresh a Power BI view and draft highlights, lowlights and asks from the validated numbers only.
  • Place the draft in Notion for the founder and finance lead to edit, approve and send.

Human checkpoint

The founder and finance lead sign off every number and every sentence before anything leaves the company. The workflow never emails investors directly.

Tools

SStripeGBGoogle BigQueryddbtMPMicrosoft Power BINNotionOOpenAIHHubSpot

Systems it connects

  • Tally, Zoho Books or QuickBooks
  • Razorpay or Stripe dashboard
  • Cap table and data room

Data & consent

Uses aggregated financial and product metrics; no customer personal data appears in the update. Access to the reporting dataset is limited to founders and finance, and each month's snapshot is preserved so past updates can be traced to their sources.

What we deliver

  • Metric definitions document
  • Reconciled monthly metrics model
  • Power BI investor view
  • Notion update template with drafted narrative

How we measure it

  • Hours to produce the update
  • Reconciliation differences outstanding
  • On-time delivery to investors
  • Definition changes per quarter
